Codex review: needs changes before merge. ## What this changes This PR adds internal verified SQLite/PostgreSQL copying, generated workboard descriptors, and a versioned export envelope. **Example:** Copy a workboard containing 1,001 cards and notification cursor 9007199254740995 between database engines. - **Before:** No verified internal cross-engine copy path exists. - **After:** The worker copies into an unpublished destination and compares canonical cells, counts, allocation facts, and catalog definitions. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | Useful approved foundations have meaningful PostgreSQL harness coverage, but the known canonical-ordering defect remains. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | This maintainer-authored PR is outside the ordinary shipped-entry-point proof gate; the supplied PostgreSQL round-trip harness exercises internal copying, and no user-facing port entry point is enabled. | | **Patch quality** | 🦪 silver shellfish **(2/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Product **Kind:** Feature · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Complete **User problem:** Existing populated workboard stores cannot yet move safely between SQLite and PostgreSQL. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored direction supplies a distinct prerequisite and explicitly defers user-facing port enablement. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Needs changes before merge - 1 item remains** Keep this useful maintainer-authored PR open; the previously reported SQLite ordering defect still blocks merge. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958` ## Before merge - [ ] **Order SQLite pages by original source keys (P2)** - The previously reported defect remains unresolved. The SQLite projection aliases JSON-escaped text to the original column names, so ORDER BY resolves to escaped output. For valid keys `a"x` and `a0x`, SQLite reads `a0x` first while PostgreSQL C ordering reads `a"x` first, causing `Port canonical verification failed`. Across page boundaries, the decoded cursor can also revisit or skip rows because filtering and ordering use different representations. Add a source-table alias, qualify SQLite ordering and cursor keys through it, and extend the PostgreSQL round trip with escaped keys spanning a page boundary. ## Findings - [P2] Order SQLite pages by original source keys — `src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:116` ### Tests - Missing end-to-end proof: The supplied round trip does not show a failing-before and passing-after regression for escaped text keys spanning a pagination boundary.
Agent review details ### How this fits together The offline worker consumes caller-owned private databases and canonical descriptors, producing an unpublished destination and verification facts for later port orchestration. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Canonical schema] --> B[Generated descriptor] B --> C[Offline copy worker] D[Private source database] --> C C --> E[Unpublished destination] E --> F[Cell and catalog verification] F --> G[Verification facts] ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Order SQLite pages by source-qualified canonical keys and cover escaped keys across page boundaries. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Source inspection establishes the escaped-key ordering failure; no target code or tests were executed during this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The foundations appropriately reuse canonical schema, SQLite primitive, and cell-encoding owners, but pagination must order original source keys. Full review comments: - [P2] Order SQLite pages by original source keys — `src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:116` The previously reported defect remains unresolved. The SQLite projection aliases JSON-escaped text to the original column names, so ORDER BY resolves to escaped output. For valid keys `a"x` and `a0x`, SQLite reads `a0x` first while PostgreSQL C ordering reads `a"x` first, causing `Port canonical verification failed`. Across page boundaries, the decoded cursor can also revisit or skip rows because filtering and ordering use different representations. Add a source-table alias, qualify SQLite ordering and cursor keys through it, and extend the PostgreSQL round trip with escaped keys spanning a page boundary. Confidence: 0.99 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.98 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [001e13bc4f7d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/001e13bc4f7d9ca3fb4c3b4437b693633769f345). ### Provenance checked - `Workboard PostgreSQL generation` keeps the original intent (5e78ec6881c277fae9d4279e9315b5a1cc4b2925: Generate canonical workboard DDL while retaining namespace and admission-transaction ownership at the connection boundary.) - `SQLite primitive ownership` keeps the original intent (30ae21fca71b56a22127b22f1462fbd002fafce3: Preserve allocation state and integrity during atomic STRICT migrations.) - `Dialect ratchet classification` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (a1c1610b1907a3750f623297af19dedd425f7399: Prevent growth in SQLite-specific constructs; this PR records an accepted exception for centralized engine-maintenance primitives.) - `Git backup cell encoding` keeps the original intent (37b4fc8621d98a3debbd2202d27f40aa039f386f: Produce deterministic versioned snapshots with lossless bigint and BLOB encoding.) - `NUL-safe Git backup serialization` keeps the original intent (a036c70ee75d246e6c5d5e874e91dc159d12d6b1: Escape text before native reads while preserving original source-column ordering.) - `Snapshot manifest parser visibility` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (c1d6d31855627b15e361dbdb41c802d6b26fd439: Keep implementation-only exports private; the new internal envelope reader now requires the existing parser.) ### Testing Proof path: in-process harness. ### Security None. ### Evidence Acceptance criteria: - node scripts/test-database-conformance.mjs --engine postgres --connection postgresql://postgres@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres -- src/infra/database-engine/port.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - pnpm test src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.test.ts --maxWorkers=1 - git diff --check What I checked: - **Unresolved ordering defect:** SQLite text projections retain original column names as aliases, and ORDER BY uses those unqualified names; decoded source keys subsequently become pagination cursors. ([`src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:116`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L116), [243996c0f1b7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958)) - **Previous finding remains:** The change since the previous reviewed head adds only an assertion-invariant comment and leaves the affected query unchanged. ([`src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:140`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L140), [243996c0f1b7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958)) - **Existing source-ordering contract:** The Git backup serializer qualifies original source keys to avoid ordering escaped aliases, preserving the NUL-safe serialization work in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/138327, reported by @ced-cm. ([`src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.ts:156`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958/src/snapshot/git-backup-codec.ts#L156), [243996c0f1b7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958)) - **Distinct foundations:** Fetched main has neither the port worker nor the export-envelope module; current reference searches find only test callers for their new APIs. ([`src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts:383`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/001e13bc4f7d9ca3fb4c3b4437b693633769f345/src/infra/database-engine/port.worker.ts#L383), [001e13bc4f7d](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/001e13bc4f7d9ca3fb4c3b4437b693633769f345)) - **Accepted ratchet classification:** The maintainer-authored body explicitly accepts the primitive-owner exception; inspection confirms that only sqlite-strict.ts is listed and only its engine-maintenance matches are excluded from comparison. ([`scripts/check-database-dialect-ratchet.mts:41`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958/scripts/check-database-dialect-ratchet.mts#L41), [243996c0f1b7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958)) - **Existing-state compatibility:** Format-1 reading delegates to the existing parser, the extracted Git cell encoding preserves its implementation, and no runtime caller activates the new envelope or copy path. ([`src/snapshot/export-envelope.ts:73`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958/src/snapshot/export-envelope.ts#L73), [243996c0f1b7](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/243996c0f1b7f3bc580638d3154ffde367045958)) Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Raw commit 5e78ec6881c277fae9d4279e9315b5a1cc4b2925 adds scripts/generate-postgres-schema.mts:17 relative to its recorded parents.
